title: Level-one weight of the minority indicator
statement: Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, and define $h(x)$ to be $(1-f(x))/2$ if the uniform mean of $f$ is nonnegative, and $(1+f(x))/2$ otherwise. The level-one Fourier weight of $f$ is four times the level-one Fourier weight of $h$, where level-one weight is the sum of squared Fourier coefficients over singleton coordinate sets.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
